messages:
sara: heads up — customers reporting intermittent 502/504s and large latency spikes for hosted inference in eu-central-az2. lots of requests timing out at the gateway (~10–30% error rate). first seen ~09:15 UTC.

devon: confirming, I'm seeing the same in edge metrics. error percent for /v1/generate jumped from ~0.3% -> 18% at 09:14. traces show upstream read_timeouts and TCP retransmits to the hosting nodes.

mike: customer-facing: CS_4521 pinged — several customers have open support tickets with replayed cURLs getting 502. example: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'` returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway. request-id header present: req-0a1b2c3d.

anna: posted to customers that we're investigating and suggested retry/backoff for now. any quick mitigations? :pray:

devon: running quick network checks. traceroute from our frontends to model hosts shows packet loss starting at AS64500 (transit partner) hops 6–8:

```
traceroute to host-az2-01 (10.2.5.18), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  gw-az2-int (10.2.0.1)  0.6 ms
 2  pop-eu (198.51.100.1)  1.2 ms
 3  transit-a (203.0.113.5)  18.3 ms  * *  (30% packet loss)
 4  transit-a (203.0.113.6)  22.1 ms  * *  (40% packet loss)
 5  host-az2-01 (10.2.5.18)  23.4 ms
```

devon: also `ss -n` on the host shows lots of retransmits and `RTO` increases. kernel logs with repeated `TCP: time wait` and retransmit messages.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-1207-az2-net. Pager escalation to eng-oncall if >15% error persists for 15m.

mike: opened P1 with transit provider (ticket TKT-9981). included captures: pcap snippets, flow logs, and BGP state snapshots. provider initial response: 'we're seeing flapping on a peering session, investigating'.

devon: quick mitigation options: 1) reroute external egress to eu-central-az3 for new requests, 2) enable temporary regional fallback in smart routing policy to prefer eu-central-az1/az3, 3) push canary model pool to az3 and shift read traffic. downside: capacity in az3 limited, may impact latency for some customers.

sara: initiate routing policy failover now? customers are complaining about timeouts and a couple reported auth failures due to repeated retries exhausting token caches. high priority.

eng-oncall: I'm on it. shifting API traffic for hosted inference routes away from eu-central-az2 (set route tag prefer=eu-central-az3 for 20m) and enabling extra connection retries (2 -> 4) while decreasing per-connection timeout to keep latency bounded. doing a staged 10% -> 50% -> 100% shift.

anna: CS notified customers for whom we have on-call paging: queued guidance: allow retries with exponential backoff, watch for duplicate billing charges (we will suppress duplicate bill events for requests during incident window).

devon: after 10% shift we already see error percent drop to ~8%, after 50% shift down to 3.5%. packetloss to az2 still present on traceroutes. provider updated: BGP flaps fixed on one session but second path showing asymmetry and packet drops, suspect transit engine microbursts.

mike: ran repro with `grpcurl` and sample payloads against az3 endpoint — stable, latency as expected ~40–70ms. pushing failover to 100% for hosted inference write/read traffic to az3 now. note: any stateful sessions pinned to az2 will still see issues — working on drain policy for pinned KV caches.

eng-oncall: drain started. command used: `redwoodctl routes update --service hosted-inference --from eu-central-az2 --to eu-central-az3 --drain 300` (300s drain). also added temporary model fallback to a quantized variant to reduce CPU time while capacity ramps.

ops-bot: Status changed -> mitigated. Monitoring for 30m before declaring resolved.

anna: CS update sent: affected window 09:14–10:12 UTC, increased 502/504 errors due to transit provider peering flaps causing packet loss and asymmetric routing to eu-central-az2. traffic rerouted to eu-central-az3, no billing duplicates observed so far; suppressed duplicate charge events between 09:20–10:30 UTC.

devon: follow-up actions: 1) collect BGP adjacency history and export to provider for RCA, 2) add probe to detect AS64500 packet loss >5% and auto-failover, 3) evaluate capacity baseline for eu-central-az3 to avoid capacity shock, 4) postmortem and customer comms draft.

sara: thanks all. filing postmortem owner tag to devon. assigning blameless RCA to eng-team-networking. will link CS ticket CS_4521 and transit ticket TKT-9981 in the postmortem.

mike: closing loop — provider acknowledged misconfiguration on peering edge, they scheduled permanent fix + monitoring. marking incident resolved at 10:18 UTC pending RCA.

eng-oncall: final note: if you see auth token errors tied to this window, don't auto-retry in client libs — add idempotency checks. we'll put a brief note in SDK changelog.
